reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown treat Deuteronomy's Egypt motive as an added reason for the Sabbath, not a rival account replacing Exodus's creation rationale.

discrepancy.note: Paine notes Deuteronomy's fourth commandment gives a different reason for the Sabbath than Exodus does, naming the Exodus from Egypt instead of creation.

quotes.text: In that of Exodus, the reason given for keeping the seventh day is, because (says the commandment) God made the heavens and the earth in six days, and rested on the seventh; but in that of Deuteronomy, the reason given is, that it was the day on which the children of Israel came out of Egypt,
quotes.attr: Thomas Paine (d. 1809), The Age of Reason, Part II (1795), ch. I, on Exodus 20:11 and Deuteronomy 5:15.

sides.snippet: for in six days Yahweh made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them, and rested the seventh day; therefore Yahweh blessed the Sabbath day, and made it holy.
sides.verseText: for in six days Yahweh made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them, and rested the seventh day; therefore Yahweh blessed the Sabbath day, and made it holy.

sides.snippet: You shall remember that you were a servant in the land of Egypt… therefore Yahweh your God commanded you to keep the Sabbath day.
sides.verseText: You shall remember that you were a servant in the land of Egypt, and Yahweh your God brought you out of there by a mighty hand and by an outstretched arm: therefore Yahweh your God commanded you to keep the Sabbath day.
